title: Boothville gigs with Frank Crump
summary: Weekend jobs at Boothville and Buras with Frank Crump's four-piece.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: That's the way we had to communicate, you know. Let the people know we was going on down. In those days they didn't have much, no microphone, we had those, what's called those people? Yeah. Talk and sing over that. I went down there to Boothville and Burris a long time with little Frank Crump.
Oh. Uh-huh. What about the people, they speak French down there? Oh yeah. Oh I see, so they like those numbers. Everybody. Who was Frank Crump? I never met him.
I never met him. I don't know anybody.

He was an outdoor saxophone player. Frank, me, Frank Crump, John Porter, we had one time Lana of Tarragana or Albert Giles or somebody like that. We had four piece, we used to go to Boothville. Friday, Saturday, Sunday, man had a place for us to stay down there. Drink that orange wine.
